issues.title: Process: autonomous sessions cannot reach 6s-success.com or api.indexnow.org, so the IndexNow traffic lever can never close
issues.body:
## What keeps happening

Three separate passes now have hit the identical wall:

- STATUS.md, 2026-08-19: outbound proxy denies 6s-success.com with a policy 403.
- ops/NIGHTLY-LOG.md, 2026-08-21 (two orphaned articles pass): could not submit 134 regenerated pages to IndexNow because the proxy blocks both 6s-success.com and api.indexnow.org, and correctly refused to claim success it could not verify.
- This pass (2026-08-21, dashboard accuracy pass): confirmed the same block again, `curl https://6s-success.com/` returns `CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403` from this session's proxy.

Per the operating instructions, three consecutive occurrences of the same defect means stop fixing the symptom and open an issue about the process producing it. This is that issue.

## Why this is a process gap, not a one-off

The sandboxed network these autonomous sessions run in appears to allow only a fixed set of destinations (GitHub, the Anthropic proxy). It cannot reach:

- the live site, for `ops/verify_deploy.py` style checks
- `api.indexnow.org`, so `ops/indexnow.py --submit` can never complete from inside an autonomous session
- presumably the Umami analytics endpoint, so traffic data can never be pulled by an autonomous session either

Every session correctly refuses to fake success it cannot verify, which is the right behavior, but it means "submit the pages to IndexNow" and "confirm the site is reachable" have sat as "owed" across at least three passes and will keep sitting there indefinitely. 156 pages, including the 134 regenerated with the two new article links, are still not confirmed submitted.

## What I need from you

Pick one:

1. **Run it yourself once**, from a machine with normal internet: `python ops/indexnow.py --submit` from the repo root. Takes a minute, unblocks the whole backlog at once.
2. **Move it to CI**, a GitHub Action on push to main that runs `ops/indexnow.py --submit` (and optionally `ops/verify_deploy.py`) with real egress. This also fixes the recurring "site reachability: unverified" line in STATUS.md and the dashboard for good, not just for this one submission.
3. **Grant the sandboxed environment wider egress**, if that is possible on your end, though I would default to option 2 since it is fully traceable through Git rather than a standing permission.

I recommend option 2: it is the only one of the three that stops this from being a manual chore Phil has to remember, and it matches the "GitHub is the delivery control plane" principle already in CLAUDE.md.

## Not blocking today's work

This does not block content or conversion work, which does not require live egress. It only blocks closing the loop on "did the pages actually get submitted" and "is the site actually reachable," both of which remain honestly marked UNKNOWN rather than a fabricated pass.

issues.title: Decide: 6S Success and Ledgerium share one Stripe legal entity
issues.body:
## What I found

While branding the checkout page I found the 6S Success Stripe account carrying
another company's identity:

- **Business website: `https://ledgerium.ai`**
- **Product description:** Ledgerium AI's, in full, describing a workflow
  documentation platform
- **Industry: Software**, which is why the MCC is 5734, Computer Software Stores
- **Account representative email: `hello@ledgerium.ai`**

Editing them opens a dialog headed **"Shared legal entity: Changes to this legal
entity will update all accounts that use it."**

## Why it is like that, and why that part is fine

The same dialog says *"Because you selected individual as your business type,
your name is also the legal name of your business."*

So both businesses are you, personally, as a sole proprietor. They genuinely
share a legal entity because there is only one. That is not a misconfiguration,
and Stripe explicitly permits it:

> When you have multiple projects or businesses that operate under the same
> legal entity, you can use the same tax ID and business information across
> multiple accounts. Make sure to provide suitable public business information
> to avoid customer confusion.

They are also already **separate accounts**, which is the part that matters
most. This is `acct_1U5rDs6OlZmKL8mF`, and it has its own products, prices,
payment links, balance and payouts.

## On organizations

You suggested organizations, and it is the right instinct but not the fix here.
Stripe Organizations are a reporting and team-management container:

> An organization doesn't conduct its own business through Stripe. It acts as a
> container structure to view and manage the operation of its separate
> businesses.

An organization would give you one dashboard across both brands, consolidated
reports, and one place to manage team access. Genuinely useful once there are
two revenue streams to compare. It would **not** separate the legal entity or
give each brand its own business profile, because that is not what it does.

## The actual problem, which is smaller than it looked

Not the shared entity. Just the **public information on this account**, which
Stripe says must be per account precisely to avoid the confusion above.

Already fixed, and per account:

| Field | Now |
|---|---|
| Public business name | 6S Success |
| Statement descriptor | 6S SUCCESS |
| Support email | support@6s-success.com |
| Support URL | https://6s-success.com/contact |
| Privacy policy, Terms | the real pages on our site |
| Checkout icon and colours | the site's arc gauge and palette |

**Still wrong: the business website field**, which is what appears on receipts
and in a dispute review. I was blocked from editing it: overwriting a
business-identity field on a live payment account is held back by a safety
check, which I am not going to route around.

## What I need from you

1. **Change the business website to `https://6s-success.com`.**
   Settings, Business details, Public details, Edit. It sits directly under the
   support URL I already filled. **Check whether saving warns that it will
   change Ledgerium too.** If it does, stop and tell me, because that is a real
   trade and not mine to make.

2. **Rewrite the product description**, currently Ledgerium's. There is a
   correct one already written in `STRIPE.md` under "The corrected business
   description", which uses Straighten rather than Set in Order and puts Safety
   fourth.

3. **Consider changing the industry** from Software. 5734 is Computer Software
   Stores, which is wrong for books, card decks and home consulting, and MCC
   affects both interchange rates and fraud scoring. It may trigger a review, so
   it is your call rather than a quiet fix.

4. **Optional: create an organization.** Worth doing when both brands are
   earning and you want one view. Not urgent, and it does not solve any of the
   above.

## Also worth knowing

Checkout currently shows **"6S Success will contribute 1% of your purchase to
removing CO2"**. Stripe Climate is on at 1% of revenue. Keep it or turn it off,
but it should be a decision rather than an inheritance from the other account.

issues.title: Decide: how the card decks get sold, and what unblocks the paid tier
issues.body:
## What exists, verified today

**Entryway v2, 90 cards.** Fully written, 90 of 90 illustrated. **It cannot
ship.** A professional print review concluded it is "two production generations
glued together":

- The EM family is painterly illustration; EP and ET are photoreal. Fanned on a
  table the green cards look like a different product.
- A third of the cards use a back template that puts red Problem-card styling
  and an orange trophy on green Micro Zone cards, breaking the colour code.
- Two cards carry real brand logos (Amazon on EP-005 and EE-001, DYMO on
  ET-007). That is a trademark problem, not a taste problem.
- Garbled AI text baked into pixels: "scicsors", "foutwear", "UMBBELLAS", "KYYS".
- Card backs run 3 to 4pt type at 2.5 x 3.5in trim and will not survive print.
- FRONT and BACK proofing labels sit outside the trim on several cards.

Only 6 of the 18 defective images have regeneration prompts written, and
EE-001, the worst one, is not among the 6.

**Entryway v3, 46 cards.** The fix, and nearly done. Correctly sized, house
style clean (zero em dashes, zero "Set in Order", no brand names, Safety
asserted as the fourth S on all 46), and **all 46 illustration prompts already
written** against a frozen style anchor. Note it is a different art direction:
flat vector illustration aimed at children 5 to 10 and caregivers, with a
recurring character. That is a coherent choice but it is not the photoreal
direction v2 was heading toward.

**Mudroom.** One card list, 2 images. Effectively not started.

## What I shipped today, needing no decision

The v3 deck is now live and free at https://6s-success.com/deck.html and
https://6s-success.com/deck/entryway-print-and-play.html, listed in the shop,
linked from the footer of all 148 pages, and submitted to IndexNow. Every card
carries a simple line drawing, so it prints as a complete usable deck now.

I also brought 3.7 MB of deck source into the repository. It had lived only on
the Desktop with no backup and no history.

## The decision

**How the ladder should work, my recommendation:**

1. **Free print at home deck.** Live now. Costs nothing to fulfil and answers
   the actual constraint, which is that nobody is arriving at this site.
2. **Illustrated print and play PDF, about 19 dollars.** Needs the 46 images.
   Zero fulfilment cost, sellable through a Stripe payment link the day the art
   lands. **This is the fastest path to first product revenue in the whole
   estate.**
3. **Physical printed boxed deck, about 39 dollars.** Needs a print on demand
   partner. A real decision with real money, not a task.
4. **Rooms 2 through 20.** Only after the Entryway earns its keep. Building
   twenty decks before one sells would be a way of looking busy.

**The one thing that unblocks tier 2: generate 46 images.** The prompts are
written and self contained, one per card, in
`content/decks/entryway/Entryway-Illustration-Prompts-ALL.md`. Open a fresh
chat per image, paste one prompt, save the result as P1 to P46. I cannot
generate images; everything either side of that step is done or can be.

**What I recommend doing with v2:** retire it. It is 173 MB of art that a print
review says cannot ship and that v3 supersedes on every axis. The files stay on
the Desktop. Regenerating 18 images to rescue a 90 card deck that also needs a
back template rebuild and a legibility pass is more work than finishing v3.

## What I need from you

1. Confirm the ladder above, or tell me where it is wrong.
2. Decide whether v2 is retired or rescued.
3. If you want tier 2, run the 46 prompts. That is the whole blocker.

Related: #1 and #2 both concern v2 art and should be closed as superseded if
you retire it. #18 is the same class of question for the book's chapter 47.

issues.title: Chapter 39 plates promise printables that do not exist
issues.body:
## What was found

While wiring the Kids Bedroom room page I could only use 3 of chapter 39's 20
finished plates. The rest are blocked by things baked into the image itself,
which no code change can fix.

**QR codes offering resources we do not have.** Plates 05, 16 and 19 each
carry a QR code with copy like "Scan for our printable Toy Room Reset Mindset
Reminders and Wall Art" and "Scan for our Bedding Care Guide". No such
printable exists, and the codes were not generated against any real URL. On a
marketing site that is a promise we cannot keep, so I did not publish them.
I checked 6 plates in detail; the pattern starts at plate 05, so the true
count is likely higher than 3.

**A visible typo.** Plate 03, which is otherwise the strongest of the batch
because it carries real dimensional standards, reads "put at away" in its
closing line. It also has an em dash baked into the artwork.

Plates 01, 02 and 04 are clean and are now live on
https://6s-success.com/rooms/kids-bedroom

## Why this is worth a decision

This is very unlikely to be a chapter 39 problem. The same generation pass
produced chapters 31 to 38, and the existing image quality backlog already
records fake QR codes and baked em dashes across chapters 1 to 17. So the
question is not what to do about chapter 39, it is which of two things we
want:

1. **Build the printables the images already promise.** The Reset Playbook
   checklist, the timer card and the bedding care guide are all small, and we
   have the content to write them. Then point the QR codes at real URLs on the
   site. This turns a defect into a lead capture surface, though it depends on
   issue #15 being resolved first.
2. **Regenerate the affected plates without QR codes.** Cheaper and faster, but
   discards a genuinely good idea.

## Recommendation

Option 1, but not yet. Building printables is only worth it once email capture
works, and that is blocked on issue #15. Until then the plates stay unused,
which costs us nothing because the three clean ones already carry the room
page. Revisit when #15 closes.

## What I need from you

Nothing today. This is recorded so the decision is made deliberately rather
than by the plates quietly staying unused forever.

issues.title: Decide: chapter 47's 27 plates are monochrome while the rest of the book is colour
issues.body:
## What was found

Chapter 47, The Mudroom, has 27 finished plates on disk. None are wired into
the chapter and none are on the Mudroom room page. That is not an oversight:
a pass on 2026-08-05 stopped deliberately before wiring and left its reasoning
in `CH47_IMAGE_FINALIZATION_NOTES.md` in the Master folder.

I re-measured it independently today and the earlier finding holds.

Mean per pixel colour saturation:

| Batch | Saturation |
|---|---|
| Chapter 47, all 27 plates | 2.2 |
| Chapter 38, already wired | 54.5 |
| Chapter 39, wired today | 56.5 |

Every chapter 47 plate is a black and white pencil illustration. Chapters 31
to 39 are warm colour photography and colour infographics. That is an order of
magnitude apart, not a variation.

The earlier pass also found two canon violations in the plates it opened, the
clearest being that `image09` recommends a lidded basket to hide clutter,
which contradicts the chapter's own frozen argument that a lid hides the drift
instead of fixing it.

## Why this is yours and not mine

Wiring the plates would commit the book to a mixed visual style by default,
which is a whole book decision. Leaving them out keeps one of 20 rooms
unillustrated. Neither is reversible for free.

## Options

1. **Regenerate chapter 47 in the established colour style.** Keeps Part 9
   coherent. Costs one batch of image generation. This is my recommendation.
2. **Restyle the whole book to monochrome line art.** The illustrations are
   genuinely good and one colour printing is materially cheaper, but this
   orphans the nine chapters already wired plus everything in chapters 1 to 30.
3. **Keep a deliberate mixed style.** I advise against it. It reads as a
   production accident rather than a choice.

Whichever way it goes, the canon violations need fixing before those plates
are used.

## Recommendation

Option 1. The colour family is established across nine wired chapters and the
whole site design system, and one batch is the cheapest way to make chapter 47
match rather than making 40 other things match chapter 47.

issues.title: Decide: the four hour loop trigger cannot be self updated by any session
issues.body:
The four hour loop routine, trigger id `trig_011oe2y7KR3AiPxUTd6b9P6c`, was created through the http_api rather than by a Claude session. Its stored prompt is a frozen snapshot of `ops/routine-prompt.md` from the day it was created. The repository copy of that file keeps getting fixed as defects are found, but the fix never reaches the routine that actually fires, because `update_trigger` refuses any routine it did not itself create.

This is not a one off. Three separate sessions have now hit variants of the same problem:

1. 2026-08-20, session recorded in `ops/NIGHTLY-LOG.md` under "the free sample's broken images": `git checkout main` reported up to date against a stale cached ref, 49 commits behind actual `origin/main`.
2. 2026-08-20, session recorded under "linking the zone and room pages back to the articles": fixed `ops/routine-prompt.md` step 0 to fetch before checkout, but could not push the fix into the live trigger, since `update_trigger` refused it.
3. 2026-08-20, this session: started from a stale local main 28 commits behind and disconnected from origin's real history (no common ancestor), because the container's baked in git state predated a subsequent history rewrite on origin. Recovered by fetching origin directly and resetting to it. No work was actually lost, since the 50 commits in question had already reached GitHub, but the local checkout looked authoritative and was not.

Each fix has patched the symptom (the repo's copy of the step 0 instructions) rather than the underlying defect, which is that the routine's own stored prompt cannot be corrected by the agents who discover it needs correcting. The prompt that fired this very session still carried the pre fix wording, three days after the fix landed in the repository.

The options, as I see them:

1. Delete the http_api created trigger and have a Claude session recreate it with `create_trigger`, so future sessions can self maintain it with `update_trigger`. Loses the trigger's run history.
2. Keep the trigger as is, and have Phil (or whichever http_api actor created it) manually copy the current contents of `ops/routine-prompt.md` into the trigger's prompt each time it changes. Keeps history, adds a manual step that will be forgotten the same way the last two fixes were.
3. Change the routine's prompt to something that does not go stale: instead of embedding the full step by step instructions inline, have it say "read and follow `ops/routine-prompt.md` from the repository" and nothing else. Whoever can edit the trigger would only need to do it once.

My recommendation is option 3. It removes the class of defect entirely rather than relying on a human remembering to re-sync a copy, and it does not require deciding between losing run history and adding a manual step that has already been missed twice.

This needs a decision because updating the trigger is outside what any Claude session can do to its own routine, and choosing between "reset history" and "trust a manual sync" is Phil's call, not mine to make unilaterally.

issues.title: Decide: the Kitchen safety pass never mentions gas
issues.body:
## Decision

The Kitchen Cooking Zone's Safety pass never mentions gas. Decide whether it should, and how far that goes.

## What is there, and it is good

Writing the Kitchen shooting scripts surfaced this. The Cooking Zone handles fire properly:

> Turn every pan handle inward so it cannot catch a sleeve or a small hand reaching up. Keep the tea towel, the paper roll, and the oil bottle off the burner side of the hob, and know where the fire blanket or extinguisher is before a pan is smoking.

And the hazard note is specific and correct:

> Oil left heating unattended, and a tea towel or a paper roll stored within reach of a live burner, are the two ways a kitchen fire actually starts.

That is better safety writing than most of the category manages.

## What is absent

The word **gas** appears zero times in the entire Cooking Zone: not in the Safety pass, not in the hazards, not in the cleaning detail. The only adjacent mention anywhere is buried in the inspection notes as "a burner that lights slow, burns yellow and sooty".

A reader with a gas hob is being walked through cleaning around live burners, moving a hob, and reaching behind an appliance, with no mention of gas at any point. That gap is now on 114 live pages and in the manual.

## Why this is your call and not mine

Three reasons I did not simply write it in.

**It is safety copy that is already published.** Editing safety text on live pages without the owner seeing it is the wrong default, even when the edit adds rather than removes.

**Scope is genuinely arguable.** The manual explicitly disclaims instruction for gas, electrical and structural work. A reasonable position is that gas safety belongs to the gas supplier and the appliance manual, and that a home organising guide should say "not our territory, here is who to call" rather than teach it.

**It has a liability dimension.** Saying too little about gas is a gap. Saying slightly the wrong thing about gas is worse than saying nothing.

## Options

| Option | What it means |
|---|---|
| **A pointer, not instruction** | One line in the Cooking Zone Safety pass: if you smell gas, stop, do not touch switches, ventilate, leave, and call the national gas emergency line. No cleaning or maintenance guidance. |
| Full gas hazard treatment | Add gas to the hazard taxonomy across every zone with a gas appliance. More complete, considerably more surface, and drifts toward instruction we disclaim. |
| Leave it | Defensible on the grounds that gas is out of scope. It is also the option where somebody cleans a hob having read nothing about it. |

## Recommendation

**The pointer.** One sentence, no instruction, no maintenance, just the recognise-and-evacuate sequence and who to call. It closes the gap without teaching anything we have disclaimed, and it is consistent with how the manual already handles plumbing and electrics: name the hazard, then hand off to a professional.

If you agree I will write it into the Cooking Zone, regenerate the affected pages, and it flows to the manual and the shooting scripts from the same source.

## Also found while scripting, lower stakes

- The Prep Counter has no chemical hazard note even though its own cleaning detail has you using a degreaser on a food surface.
- Two Kitchen zones have no chapter reference where the other five do.
- Four of the fourteen Kitchen hazard notes reuse the identical label "Fall, cut, or crush", so the taxonomy is thinner than it looks.
- The room tips say to empty the sink zone first and hold it a week, while the tracker publish order starts at the prep counter. Not a conflict for readers, but the crew needs to shoot the sink episode first.

## Required response

Approve the pointer, choose another option, or say gas is deliberately out of scope and I will record that as a decision so it does not get raised again.

issues.title: Decide: 6S Success needs its own Listmonk, or the shared one breaks both brands
issues.body:
## Decision

One Listmonk instance now serves two businesses. Decide whether 6S Success gets its own, or whether the shared one is reconfigured.

## What I found

The `6S Success Readers` list exists and works. I subscribed a test address end to end and Listmonk accepted it and sent a confirmation. Then I read that confirmation out of the mailbox, and it would have broken every signup:

**1. The confirmation link is dead.**

```
http://localhost:9000/subscription/optin/eeb9c298-...
```

That is Listmonk's default Root URL, untouched. `localhost` resolves to the *subscriber's own machine*, so the link cannot work for anybody. With double opt-in enabled, **100 percent of signups would be unconfirmable** and the list would fill with pending addresses that can never be mailed.

**2. The sender is the wrong brand.**

```
From: "Compassion Benchmark" <info@compassionbenchmark.com>
```

Somebody who signs up on 6s-success.com receives mail from an unrelated company. That reads as phishing, and it damages both brands.

## Why it is a decision and not a fix

Root URL and the from address are **instance wide in Listmonk, not per list**. So they cannot be set correctly for two brands at once:

- Point Root URL at `6s-success.com` and every Compassion Benchmark confirmation link breaks.
- Leave it as it is and every 6S Success link stays broken.
- Change the from address either way and one of the two brands sends mail as the other.

Compassion Benchmark is a live business, so I am not touching its settings.

## Options

| Option | Cost | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| **A second Listmonk for 6S Success** | One more container, no licence cost | Each brand gets a correct Root URL and sender. Clean, and the pattern already used for the website and the MCP server. |
| Reconfigure the shared one for 6S | Free | Breaks Compassion Benchmark's confirmation links. Not acceptable. |
| Reconfigure for a neutral sender | Free | Both brands send mail as something that is neither. Worse for trust than either alone. |
| Use a hosted provider for 6S only | Free to 1,000 contacts | Reintroduces the vendor decision that Listmonk had already removed. |

## Recommendation

**A second Listmonk instance for 6S Success**, on its own port behind the proxy, with Root URL set to its public HTTPS address and the sender set to `support@6s-success.com`, which is a mailbox we already control and which already sends.

It costs one container on a VPS already running eight projects, keeps Compassion Benchmark untouched, and means neither brand can ever send mail as the other.

## What I did in the meantime

The newsletter form is **not** pointed at Listmonk. The wiring was written and then deliberately reverted, because a form that produces dead confirmation links is worse than the honest handoff that is there now. The code is in git history at the commit that records this and takes minutes to restore once the instance is correct.

Also: `support@6s-success.com` is on the list as an unconfirmed test subscriber. Harmless, and worth removing when convenient.

## Required response

Approve a second Listmonk instance, or name a different option. Once the instance has a correct Root URL and sender, wiring the form and verifying a real double opt-in end to end is one pass.

issues.title: Decide: the free sample is 40 MB and is 89 percent of the site
issues.body:
## Decision

The free sample PDF is 40 MB after optimisation. Decide whether to cut it further, and how.

## Why this is on your desk

The sample is the lead magnet. It is the first thing a reader is asked to download, before they trust us with anything, and it is **89 percent of the entire deployable website** by size. Everything else on the site, all 14 pages, every image, the whole design system, comes to under 5 MB together.

Today it was reduced from 50.7 MB to 40.0 MB with no loss of quality: five images had been saved in a lossless format meant for line art rather than photographs, and re-encoding them at identical pixel dimensions removed 7.4 MB. The remaining 168 images are already efficiently encoded. There is no more free ground.

Going below 40 MB means trading image quality, and that is a product decision rather than a cleanup.

## The options, measured

| Option | Result | What is lost |
|---|---|---|
| Leave it at 40 MB | No further work | A 40 MB download on a phone. Some readers will abandon it. |
| Resize images to 1200px wide | Roughly 27 MB | Slightly softer images on high density screens. Most readers would not notice. |
| Resize to 1200px and re-encode at lower quality | Roughly 24 MB | Visible softening if a reader zooms. |
| Split into two files, chapters 1 to 15 and 16 to 30 | Two files near 20 MB | Nothing in quality. Adds a second click and a second decision for the reader. |
| Offer the EPUB as the primary sample | 0.8 MB | Nothing. EPUB reflows and suits phones far better than a fixed page PDF. Some readers still expect a PDF. |

## Recommendation

**Lead with the EPUB and keep the PDF as the secondary option.** The EPUB is 0.8 MB against 40 MB, already built, already carries the cover, and passes all 32 structural checks. A fixed 492 page A4 layout is the wrong format for a phone regardless of file size, and a reflowing format is simply the better reading experience.

If a PDF must stay primary, resize to 1200 pixels. That is the option with the best ratio of megabytes saved to quality lost.

## What was also corrected today

The sample described itself as **"The Complete Book"** while containing chapters 1 to 30 of 50, in three places: the PDF metadata title, the HTML title tag, and the HTML page heading. Those are fixed. The claim also appears in the PDF's own rendered title page, which cannot be edited without regenerating the PDF from source, and regenerating needs a headless browser that is not installed here. Whichever option you choose above will require that regeneration anyway, so the two should be done together.

## Required response

Pick an option. If it is the EPUB, the book page is rewired in one pass and the PDF stays as a secondary link.

issues.title: Decide: model for the four-hour autonomous loop, Sonnet or Opus
issues.body:
## Decision

Should the four-hour autonomous loop run on Opus rather than Sonnet?

## Why now

The routine `6S Success four-hour work loop` went live 2026-08-17 and fires six times a day. It is currently set to `claude-sonnet-5`, which is the default carried over from the never-created nightly config in `ops/nightly-routine.json`. That default was chosen before there was any evidence about what the passes actually do.

The evidence now says the passes are not mechanical. Recent ones have involved judgement calls a cheaper model may get wrong in ways that are expensive to find later:

- Deciding that 481 of 483 em dashes were labels wanting a colon rather than prose wanting a comma. The first classification attempt was wrong about 10 of them, and only reading every case caught it.
- Noticing that a cover using the general palette put Safety in blue when every other 6S surface shows amber.
- Noticing that `can_take_payment` was hardcoded `False` behind an expression shaped like a measurement.

None of those were the assigned task. All three were caught by looking sideways at the work.

## Recommendation

**Leave it on Sonnet for one week, then decide from the log rather than from intuition.** The nine-step prompt now front-loads every gate, so a weaker pass should fail loudly rather than silently ship something wrong. Read seven days of `ops/NIGHTLY-LOG.md`, specifically the "Did not go well" sections, and switch to Opus if the failures are judgement failures rather than mechanical ones.

## Alternatives

- **Switch to Opus now.** Better work per pass, six passes a day, materially higher cost with no measurement to justify it yet.
- **Split it.** Sonnet for the four overnight passes, Opus for the 06:50 pass that feeds the 8AM debrief. More configuration to maintain, two routines to keep in sync.

## Cost and risk

Sonnet risk is a pass that produces plausible but wrong work, which the gates should catch and the retro should record. Opus risk is purely spend. Neither is irreversible: the model is one field on the routine and changes take effect on the next fire.

## Required response

Either "leave it" (no action needed, revisit 2026-08-24) or a model name. Reply in this issue.

issues.title: Two different documents both named EXECUTIVE-DASHBOARD
issues.body:
The operating system install included two files with the same name that are **not versions of each other**. Neither is a superset: 133 headings versus 140, with genuinely different content.

- `EXECUTIVE-DASHBOARD.md` (at root): Claude Current Mission, Executive Action Buttons, Global Pause, Drill-Down Pages, Dashboard Data Contract, Current Dashboard State
- `_review/EXECUTIVE-DASHBOARD-ALT.md` (parked): Revenue Mix, Revenue Definition, Customer Outcome Definition, Qualified Visitor Definition, Conversion Definition, Experiment Guardrails

Merge, keep both under distinct names, or discard one.

issues.title: Decide: keep or discard the 2,786-card master plan
issues.body:
`6S_Success_Home_Quest_Master_Plan_and_Card_Appendix.html` appeared on 13 August. Its canon defect is now fixed (891 "Set in Order" swept to "Straighten"), so it is safe either way.

The recommendation from the games review is **do not build on it**:

- It invents **212 micro zones** against the Field Manual's **114**
- Its 2,844 rows reduce to a few hundred unique strings, because eight boilerplate sentences repeat once per zone
- This is the exact waste the v3 card architecture removed, reintroduced at four times the scale

Keep, or quarantine?

issues.title: Fill in front matter bracketed fields and get counsel review
issues.body:
`6S-Success-Front-Matter/FRONT_MATTER.md` and `DISCLAIMER_BLOCK.html` are drafted and marked DRAFT / NOT LEGAL ADVICE. No shipped 6S artefact previously carried a copyright page or safety disclaimer.

**Needed from Phil:** author name, rights holder, imprint, year, ISBNs (paperback and ebook), designer, illustrator, publisher address and contact.

**Needed from counsel:** the whole Important Notice section, plus the nine other items listed for professional review in the estate review, including the "6S" trademark position against generic 5S/Lean terminology.

issues.title: Regenerate 16 remaining stale card images
issues.body:
17 of 90 Entryway card images were not regenerated in the 30 July pass. Known defects still live in pixels:

- Garbled AI text: "scicsors", "foutwear", "UMBBELLAS", "KYYS"
- A fake QR code on EM-005
- The retired friction meter on 6 EP cards
- "Set in Order" baked into 11 card faces (the text sweep cannot reach pixels)

The clearest single artefact of the drift: `ES-002-Entryway-Straighten.png` is correctly named while its card label read "Set in Order" until the sweep on 14 August. The picture and the text disagreed about the name of the second S.

issues.title: Regenerate EE-001 and EP-005 card art to remove Amazon trademarks
issues.body:
Text and filenames are fixed. **The pictures are not.**

- **EE-001** carried the card name "Amazon Delivery" burned into the artwork at roughly 60pt on both faces, with the smile-arrow logo. Renamed to "Delivery Day" in the card list, master proof, master plan and ALT text, and the file is now `EE-001-Entryway-Delivery-Day.png`, but the pixels still show the trademark.
- **EP-005** has at least five legible Amazon smile-arrows. Flagged twice on 30 July; the file timestamp is 15 minutes *before* that review, so it was never regenerated. 73 of 90 images were redone and this was one of 17 missed.

The regeneration prompt already exists at `6S-Success-Card-Decks/prompts/entryway-regeneration-prompts.md` and has never been run.

**Until this is done the Entryway deck cannot ship in any form.**
